subject: General Knowledge
topic: Indian cities on rivers — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Surat, the diamond-cutting capital of the world, is situated on the banks of which river?

options.option_text: Narmada river flowing westward through central Gujarat
Tapi (Tapti) river emptying into the Arabian Sea near Surat
Sabarmati river passing through Ahmedabad city
Mahi river draining southward into the Gulf of Khambhat

questions.explanation: Surat is on the Tapi (Tapti) river, near its mouth at the Arabian Sea. A common mistake is to pick Narmada, which also flows westward in Gujarat but passes through Bharuch (Broach), not Surat. Sabarmati is associated with Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar.

questions.stem: Ayodhya, one of India's seven sacred cities (Sapta Puri), stands on the banks of which river?

options.option_text: Yamuna, on whose western bank the city of Mathura stands
Ganga, the holiest river flowing through Varanasi and Prayagraj
Sarayu (Saryu), flowing through the Faizabad–Ayodhya region
Gomti, on whose banks Lucknow and Jaunpur are situated

questions.explanation: Ayodhya (Uttar Pradesh) is on the Sarayu (also called Saryu or Ghaghra upstream). Ganga is the most frequent distractor but it flows through Varanasi and Prayagraj, not Ayodhya. Gomti flows through Lucknow.

questions.stem: The Kumbh Mela held at Nashik draws millions of pilgrims to the banks of which river, earning Nashik the status of a sacred Kumbh site?

options.option_text: Godavari, often called the 'Ganga of the South' in religious texts
Pravara, a tributary that joins the Godavari downstream of Nashik
Tapi, flowing westward across the northern part of Maharashtra
Bhima, a major left-bank tributary of the Krishna river

questions.explanation: Nashik's Kumbh Mela (Simhastha) is held on the Godavari at the Panchavati ghats — making it one of four Kumbh sites alongside Prayagraj, Haridwar, and Ujjain. Pravara is nearby but the Kumbh is specifically on the Godavari. Tapi flows through Dhule and Bhusawal, not Nashik.

questions.stem: Cuttack, Odisha's 'Silver City' celebrated for its silver filigree craft, is a natural island city formed by the bifurcation of which river system?

options.option_text: Subarnarekha and Budhabalanga rivers merging near Balasore
Mahanadi splitting into its main channel and the Kathajodi distributary
Brahmani and Baitarani converging to form a shared delta region
Rushikulya river bifurcating near the Ganjam coastal district

questions.explanation: Cuttack is an island city sitting between the Mahanadi and its distributary the Kathajodi. The Brahmani–Baitarani pair forms a separate delta to the north; Subarnarekha drains Jharkhand into the Bay of Bengal near Balasore — both are common Odisha river distractors.

questions.stem: Ujjain, a Jyotirlinga site and the venue of the Simhastha Kumbh Mela, is situated on the banks of which river?

options.option_text: Narmada, the westward-flowing sacred river of Madhya Pradesh
Chambal, originating from the Vindhya ranges in Madhya Pradesh
Shipra (Kshipra), the holy river of western Madhya Pradesh
Betwa, a Yamuna tributary flowing past Orchha and Jhansi

questions.explanation: Ujjain (ancient Avantika) is on the Shipra (Kshipra) river. Narmada is the most common wrong pick — it passes through Jabalpur and Omkareshwar, not Ujjain. Chambal flows through Kota (Rajasthan). The Simhastha Kumbh at Ujjain is held when Jupiter enters Leo (Simha).

questions.stem: Srirangapatna (Seringapatam), the island fortress-capital of Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, is formed by a bifurcation of which river — and in which present-day Karnataka district does it lie?

options.option_text: Tungabhadra river's island near Hosapete, Vijayanagara district
Kaveri (Cauvery) river forming the island in Mandya district, Karnataka
Krishna river's bifurcation near the Andhra Pradesh border
Sharavati river gorge downstream of Jog Falls, Shivamogga district

questions.explanation: Srirangapatna is an island in the Kaveri river, located in Mandya district. The Kaveri splits into two channels here, creating a natural fortress island — a key strategic advantage for Tipu Sultan. Tungabhadra and Hampi (Vijayanagara) are frequent distractors for Karnataka river-history questions.

questions.stem: Among the following river–city pairings, which one is INCORRECTLY matched?

options.option_text: Dibrugarh (Assam) — situated on the Brahmaputra's southern bank
Thrissur (Kerala) — Periyar river flowing through the city centre
Kota (Rajasthan) — Chambal river cutting through the city
Nashik (Maharashtra) — Godavari at the Panchavati pilgrimage ghats

questions.explanation: Thrissur is NOT on the Periyar. The Periyar flows through Ernakulam district (past Aluva/Kochi), not Thrissur. Thrissur city is associated with the Karuvannur and Chalakudy river systems. The other three pairs are correct: Dibrugarh–Brahmaputra, Kota–Chambal, and Nashik–Godavari are all accurate and PYQ-frequent.
